Single workflow release.yml, 44 lines, read in full. It has real quality steps — "Typecheck" `pnpm typecheck` (:33) and "Lint" `pnpm lint` (:36) — but I opened package.json and they resolve to `tsc --noEmit` (package.json:10) and `eslint src/` (package.json:11): bare invocations of npm-installed tools with no repo-authored logic, which the prereg excludes from M1. AMBIGUITY DISCLOSED: `pnpm run x` is structurally a wrapper dispatching to repo-local config, like the enumerated `make z`, but it is not itself enumerated and resolves to a bare installed tool, so per the instruction to mark false when unsure I did not count it. COUNTERFACTUAL for re-aggregation: if pnpm wrappers counted, this repo would be M1=true AND M3=yes — `eslint src/` at package.json:11 is scoped to src/ only, while the build entrypoint build.mjs (referenced package.json:7-9) sits at the repo root and is never linted, under a step named simply "Lint". STRONGEST SUBSTANTIVE NEUTERING IN THE SAMPLE, though M2=false under the frozen definitions: release.yml:4-6 triggers only on `push: tags: v*`, so the repo's ONLY lint and typecheck steps never run on a push to the default branch or on any pull request — they fire only at release time, after the code has already landed. This is a trigger filter, not one of the four enumerated M2 forms (`continue-on-error`, trailing `|| true`, trailing `exit 0`, or an `if:` that never runs on default), and counting it would be consistent neither with how I treated the `paths:` filters on pingerr and HinetPy nor with the frozen text, so it is recorded here rather than counted.
